title: Phase 3 · Stage 11: Pattern matching
summary: Rewrite the command dispatcher as one switch expression over list patterns, and use property and relational patterns for status and overdue notes.

steps.title: Matching the shape of a command
body: Every handler starts the same way: split into words, check how many there are, print a usage error if it is wrong. **List patterns** let the dispatcher match the *shape* of the input and pull out the pieces in one go:
("lend", [var isbn, var id]) => Lend(isbn, id),       // exactly two words
("advance", [var n]) when int.TryParse(n, out int days) && days >= 1 => Advance(days),

A **switch expression** produces a value, so the dispatcher returns the text to print and the loop does one `Console.WriteLine`. Arms are tried top to bottom; `_` matches anything. Other patterns you will use:
{ AvailableCopies: 0 } => "every copy is out",                     // property pattern
{ AvailableCopies: var n, TotalCopies: var t } when n == t => "...", // with a guard
if (ParseTier(text) is not MemberTier tier) return "Error: ...";       // type pattern on a nullable

code: foreach (var input in new[] { "lend 1 2", "lend 1", "shelve 1 A3", "quit now" })
steps.explain: `..` matches any number of remaining elements. The first arm needs exactly three; `["lend", ..]` takes every other line that starts with `lend`.

steps.prompt: Match each pattern to what it matches.
steps.explain: Patterns compose: a list pattern can contain property patterns, and any arm can add a `when` guard.

steps.prompt: A `switch` expression tries arms top to bottom. Put these arms in an order where every arm can still be reached.
lines: { AvailableCopies: var n, TotalCopies: var t } when n == t => "every copy is on the shelf",
steps.explain: Specific arms first, the catch-all last. Put `_` first and the compiler reports the other arms as unreachable.

steps.title: A dispatcher made of patterns
prompt: Rewrite the top-level command handling around one switch expression. Everything must print what it printed before, except where this list says otherwise.

1. `string Handle(string command, string rest)` returns the text to print, using `(command, words) switch` with list patterns. The loop prints its result inside the safety net. Handlers that printed several lines now **return** them joined with `\n` (`PrintBooks` becomes `FormatBooks`, and so on).

2. Handlers take the parts they need, for example `Lend(string isbn, string id)`, `Shelve(string isbn, string? shelf)`, `FineMessage(string days, string? tier)`, `AddBook(string[] parts)`, `Join(string[] parts)`.
3. Replace `TryParseTier` with `MemberTier? ParseTier(string text)` written as a switch expression on the lower-cased text, and test it with `is not MemberTier tier`.
4. New command `status <isbn>`, written with property patterns:
- `The Hobbit: every copy is out` / `The Hobbit: every copy is on the shelf` / `The Hobbit: 2 of 3 on the shelf`,
- unknown: `Error: no book with ISBN 999`; usage: `Error: use status <isbn>`.
5. Overdue notes use a relational pattern on the days late, in both `loans` and `info`: up to 7 days ` (overdue)`, more than 7 ` (long overdue)`.
6. `help`: `Commands: add, list, find, info, shelve, status, authors, join, members, member, lend, return, renew, loans, policies, today, advance, fines, pay, stats, fine, help, quit`.
Shelfwise v1. Type help for commands.

require.message: Overdue notes use a relational pattern
Checks the parsed tier with a type pattern

hints: Start with `Handle`: copy each `case` into an arm. Commands with arguments get two arms, the right shape first (`("lend", [var isbn, var id]) => Lend(isbn, id),`) and the usage error second (`("lend", _) => "Error: ..."`).

Turn each printing method into one that builds a `List<string>` and returns `string.Join("\n", output)` (or the *empty* message). `FormatBooks` is one line: `list.Count == 0 ? whenEmpty : string.Join("\n", list)`.
`Status` is `library.Catalog.Find(isbn) switch { null => ..., { AvailableCopies: 0 } book => ..., { AvailableCopies: var n, TotalCopies: var total } book when n == total => ..., var book => ... }`.
